claims.statement: `GET /accounts/holdings` paginates positions, not accounts or holdings rows: `PositionRepository.get_by_user` counts `PositionModel` rows joined to the user's `AccountModel` rows and fetches one offset/limit window of them, so the response `total` is a position count and one account can contribute several items whose rows may be split across page boundaries because the service only ever regroups the fetched page.

`PositionService.get_user_holdings` buckets the repository's page by `account_id`, resolves each distinct account once through `AccountService.get_account` (not once per position), converts each position via `_calculate_holdings` with the caller's display currency, and then layers account context onto the already-converted rows with `UserHoldingRead(**holding.model_dump(), account_id=account.id, account_name=account.name)`.

`PositionService.get_account_holdings` walks the account's positions twice — an unlimited `PositionRepository.get_by_account` call feeds the totals while the paginated call feeds `items` — so `total_value`, `total_profit_loss`, `total_profit_loss_percent` and `profit_loss_basis` cover every position of the account while the returned `items` are a single page; the response also carries `account_id`, `account_name`, `currency`, `net_deposits`, `free_cash`, `broker_value`, `broker_value_at`, `unpriced_positions` and `pricing_incomplete`.

`HoldingRead` is triple-denominated — native (`security_currency`, `unconverted_total_value`, `unconverted_profit_loss`), account currency (`total_value`, `profit_loss`, `currency`, `converted_average_cost`, `converted_latest_price`) and display currency (`display_total_value`, `display_currency`) — `UserHoldingRead` adds `account_id`/`account_name`, `AccountHoldingRead` mirrors the display pair, and `AccountHoldingsRead` extends `PaginatedResponse[HoldingRead]` with account identity, `total_value`, `total_profit_loss`, `total_profit_loss_percent`, `profit_loss_basis`, `net_deposits`, `free_cash`, `broker_value`, `broker_value_at`, `currency`, `unpriced_positions` and `pricing_incomplete`.

Authorization differs per holdings endpoint: `GET /accounts/holdings` and `GET /accounts/holdings/{security_id}` are scoped implicitly by the repository's join on `AccountModel.user_id`, whereas `GET /accounts/{account_id}/holdings` and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` look the account up through `AccountRepository.get` and call `authorization_api.check_entity_owned_by_user` before delegating to `PositionService`.

`_calculate_holdings` handles an unresolvable security by logging `Security not found for position ...`, incrementing `unpriced_positions` and continuing, so a holdings page can return fewer rows than the position count in `total`; a position whose security resolves but has no stored price takes the other branch and is still returned as a row with `total_value=0` and `profit_loss=None` while being excluded from value, cost and P/L.

`PositionService.get_holdings_by_security` fills the repository's `AccountHoldingRead` placeholder rows (`total_value=0.0`, `currency=""`, `display_total_value=0.0`, `display_currency=""`) with `quantity × latest close` in the security currency, a `display_total_value` converted into the request's display currency (defaulting to each account's currency), `account_total_value` from `get_total_for_account` and `account_percentage` computed from the account-currency conversion only when the account total is positive, resolving the account once per returned row; an unknown security returns an ambiguous `([], 0)` that the source marks with a TODO.

The `/holdings` load reads the query-string filter ids and issues three concurrent SSR reads — `getPreferences`, `getPortfolios` and `getAccounts` — under `Promise.allSettled`: a single rejection only leaves that slot at its fallback (`normalizeHoldingsTableConfig(null)`, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode(null)`, `null` waves or an empty list), while a rejected result whose reason is an `ApiError` with status 401 clears the auth cookie and throws a 303 redirect to `/auth/login?clear_session=true` which the surrounding `catch` re-throws. The load returns `holdings_table_config`, `group_mode`, `elliott_waves`, `portfolios`, `accounts`, `portfolio_id` and `account_id`, and it never awaits or returns holdings rows.

SSR requests pass the `auth_token` cookie explicitly as a Bearer override because `ApiClient.get` only sets `Authorization: Bearer` when a token override is supplied (it always sets `credentials: 'include'`); the `/` and `/accounts/[id]` loads map a 401 to `deleteAuthCookie` plus a 303 redirect to `/auth/login?clear_session=true`, other `ApiError` statuses to Kit errors and anything else to a 500, and the `/holdings` load maps a 401 from any of its three SSR reads the same way, while its post-navigation 401 is routed through `redirectOn401`, which `goto`s `/auth/login?clear_session=true` without deleting the httpOnly cookie client-side (`hooks.server.ts` clears it when the login page resolves).

`/holdings` derives its header totals from the per-account `GET /accounts/{id}/totals` wave rather than from the row fields: the page feeds the filtered accounts' cached `AccountTotals` into `aggregateAccountTotals`, which produces one bucket per account currency (never summing across currencies), sums `value` and `profit_loss`, uses `sum(profit_loss) / sum(net_deposits)` only when every account in the bucket reports the `net_deposits` basis and otherwise labels the bucket `mixed basis` with denominator `sum(value − profit_loss)`, and yields a null percentage for a zero denominator.

`groupHoldings` in `stock` mode (and its legacy `company` alias) keys strictly on `security_id`, keeps first-appearance ordering, sums `quantity`/`display_total_value`/`unconverted_total_value` and null-preserving P/L, computes quantity-weighted `average_cost` and `converted_average_cost`, and dedupes `account_names` while counting distinct accounts; a group whose rows all share one currency keeps that currency and sums native `total_value` and P/L, while a mixed-currency group's `total_value` becomes the summed `display_total_value`, its `currency` comes from the rows' `display_currency` (falling back to `'CAD'`) and its `profit_loss` is forced to `null`.

The `/holdings` page owns its `HoldingsService` instance instead of reading a layout context: it constructs the service and seeds the group mode with `setGroupBy(data.group_mode)`, then runs three effects — one re-applying the URL filter from `data.portfolio_id`/`data.account_id`, one triggering `service.load()` once per mount, and one driving `service.loadAccountTotals(...)` for `filteredAccounts` inside `untrack`; toggling grouping and changing the portfolio/account filter are therefore client-side derivations that never refetch holdings rows (the filter does re-run the totals wave), and `getHoldingsService` remains the context/custom-fetch accessor.

`HoldingsService.load()` is the sole implementation of the collect-every-page contract: it loops `getUserHoldings(offset, PAGE_SIZE, token)` sequentially with `PAGE_SIZE = 50` and the `MAX_PAGES = 100` stale-total cap, breaks early on an empty page, stores the collected rows through the `rows` setter into `allRows`, then makes one batched `getValuationsBatch` read for the distinct security ids in its own nested `try/catch` that degrades to an empty map (also when there are no securities), toggles `isLoading` around the whole loop, never throws (it stores the message in `errorMessage`, keeps the previously loaded rows, and returns the caught error or `null`), and clears the error on the next success.

`holdings-table.svelte` stays presentational: it derives a normalized `HoldingsTableConfig` from the `tableConfig` prop, keeps a local copy so a column drag gives immediate feedback, and emits the final clamped config once at pointer-up via `onConfigChange`, while the `/holdings` page owns persistence and pushes write failures into a `holdings-error` alert without reverting the optimistic UI change.

`holdings_table` and `holdings_group` are persisted one top-level key at a time (`patchPreferences({ holdings_table: config })` / `patchPreferences({ holdings_group: mode })`) through an injected structural prefs service instead of the module singleton, matching the backend's top-level JSONB `||` merge so a concurrent write to a different preference key cannot be dropped (nested values of the same key remain last-write-wins).

`normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` guarantees a usable config from any stored shape: non-object/missing input yields defaults, unknown column ids are dropped from `widths` and `visible`, widths are clamped by `clampColumnWidth` (non-finite falls back to the default), surviving `visible` ids are re-ordered to canonical `HOLDINGS_TABLE_COLUMN_IDS` order with the sticky column force-included, an empty or fully invalid `visible` list falls back to all columns, and the returned object never aliases the defaults.

`HOLDINGS_TABLE_STICKY_COLUMN_ID` (`security_symbol`) can never be hidden: `toggleColumnVisibility` returns the same config object unchanged for it, the display-settings menu item is `disabled`, `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` re-adds it to any stored `visible` list, the table renders its first data cell with the sticky position classes whenever that column is visible, and the loading skeleton cells key their sticky styling off the constant.

`normalizeHoldingsGroupMode` normalizes the persisted `holdings_group` value to `'stock'` only for `'stock'` and the legacy `'company'`, and to `'none'` for every other value (including `'STOCK'`, numbers, objects and `null`), so a stored legacy mode still renders grouped while the next save writes `'stock'`.

`AccountClient.getAccountHoldings(id, token)` sends no `offset`/`limit`, so `/accounts/[id]` receives the backend defaults (offset 0, limit 50 for `PaginationParams`) while `AccountHoldingsRead.total` and the header totals cover every position of the account, meaning accounts with more than 50 positions render truncated rows next to complete totals.

The accounts dashboard `/` reads only the account list (`GET /accounts/`, ordered by account name) in its server load and defers each row's value to a browser-only `GET /accounts/{id}/totals` call rendered through the shared `TotalProfitLossButtons` with the basis label taken from `totals.basis` and an amber warning when `totals.pricing_incomplete`; expanding a row lazily fetches `GET /accounts/{id}/holdings` into the same per-account cache and renders the lightweight account inline holdings table, and `invalidateCache` clears both caches and re-fetches when a sync finishes.

`/accounts/[id]` renders its header from `AccountHoldingsRead` and its body through the separate presentational `frontend/src/lib/components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte`, which takes `holdings` and `totalAccountValue`, has no column configuration or grouping, shows native- and account-currency values side by side when they differ, and is mounted only when `data.holdings.items.length > 0`.

The holdings read path's test suites follow the repository's mocking contract: the frontend suites mock every API client and framework module that performs network or browser work (`$lib/api/accountService`, `$lib/api/accountClient`, `$lib/api/marketService`, `$lib/api/valuationClient`, `$lib/api/userPreferencesService`, `$app/paths`, `$app/navigation`) and never call the backend, pinning the preference-and-metadata-only load and its paging absence, the `HoldingsService` paging loop, stale-total guards and account-totals cache, per-currency bucket aggregation from the server totals, grouping and column toggles, the `redirectOn401` path, the URL-driven portfolio/account filter and single-key preference writes; the backend suites mock every outbound dependency (`PositionRepository`, `AccountService`, `SecurityApi`, `MarketPricesApi`) and pin user isolation, position pagination, per-account stamping and the pricing-completeness counters.

The `/holdings` read path is split into waves: the SSR load returns only `holdings_table_config`, `group_mode`, `elliott_waves`, `portfolios`, `accounts`, `portfolio_id` and `account_id` (and a test asserts `getUserHoldings` is never called from the load), a browser-only `$effect` then drives `HoldingsService.load()` to page every position and batch-load valuations, a third `$effect` drives the per-account totals wave for the filtered accounts, and user interactions afterwards issue single-key `PATCH /accounts/me/preferences` writes or a `goto(..., { replaceState: true })` URL update for the filter — so the shell paints skeletons before any holdings request and the page survives a failed load, totals read or preference write with an in-page `holdings-error` alert.

Both account-scoped totals surfaces share one basis rule by construction: `get_account_holdings` and `get_total_for_account` both run `_calculate_holdings` and then `_account_performance`, which adds the converted `free_cash` to `cost` and `value` and picks between the `net_deposits` basis (`profit_loss = value − net_deposits`, percentage over net deposits) and the `cost` basis (`positions_value − positions_cost`, percentage over positions cost), so the `/holdings` header (which aggregates those same server totals per currency), the `/accounts/[id]` header and the dashboard badge agree; the per-row `profit_loss` in the table body remains the cost-basis figure `value − quantity × average_cost`, so a net-deposits account shows a cash-flow header over cost-basis rows and deposits or withdrawals move the header without any position changing.

`HoldingsService` models the `/holdings` filter as a discriminated `HoldingsFilter` union (`all` | `portfolio` with `portfolioId` and `accountIds` | `account` with `accountId`) with `filterByPortfolio` / `filterByAccount` / `clearFilter` setters, and its `rows` getter narrows `allRows` by an `account_id` membership test. The page mirrors the selection by calling `goto('/holdings?portfolio_id=…' | '/holdings?account_id=…', { replaceState: true })` (and `goto('/holdings')` to clear), including from a holding's account badge through `onAccountClick`, so the URL is the source of truth for the load's filter parameters and no holdings rows are refetched on a filter change; the options come from the load's settled `portfolios` and `accounts` reads, and when the filter yields nothing while `allRows` is non-empty the page shows a filter-specific empty message.

Both non-account-scoped holdings handlers resolve the caller's stored display currency with `UserApi.get_display_currency` (default `CAD`) and pass it into `PositionService.get_user_holdings` / `get_holdings_by_security`, so every returned row carries `display_total_value`/`display_currency` converted from the account currency on top of its native and account-currency fields.

`_calculate_holding` computes the native value in the position currency (`position.currency`, falling back to `security.currency`), converts it into the account currency for `total_value`/`profit_loss`/`converted_average_cost`/`converted_latest_price`, and then converts that account-currency value again into the display currency for `display_total_value`, while `_unpriced_holding` leaves `total_value` and `display_total_value` at `0.0` with `profit_loss=None` and still reports the converted average cost.

`unpriced_positions` (a missing security or a missing price) flows into `pricing_incomplete = unpriced_positions > 0` on both `AccountTotals` and `AccountHoldingsRead`, and both the account page header and each dashboard row render an amber 'Incomplete pricing' tooltip from that flag, so a partially priced account is visibly flagged rather than silently understated.

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` accepts an optional `currency` query parameter that is trimmed, upper-cased, restricted to `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES` (`CAD`, `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`) with a 422 for anything else and defaults to the account's own currency; `AccountClient.getAccountTotals(id, token, currency?)` exposes it, while the dashboard calls it without a currency so its badge stays in the account currency.

`holdings-table.svelte` derives the portfolio total, the `Allocation` column's percent-of-total and each account badge's percent-of-account from `display_total_value` (through `calculatePercentOfTotal` / `calculatePercentOfAccount`), so shares stay comparable across accounts whose native currencies differ and are never computed by adding native values.

The `valuation_range` column is fed by the service's `valuations` map, opens an in-table `ValuationModal`, and writes a saved range back through `onValuationChange` into `service.valuations`, so the column updates without a page reload; it sorts by the midpoint of its lower/upper bounds, and its visibility and width persist in the `holdings_table` preference.

`HoldingsService.loadAccountTotals` deduplicates the requested ids, skips accounts already present in its `accountTotals` cache and returns `null` without a request when nothing is missing, fetches the rest in parallel with `Promise.allSettled` against `AccountClient.getAccountTotals`, stores each fulfilled result by id, and records only the first rejection's message in `errorMessage` — so a filter change only pays for uncached accounts and one unreachable account loses a header bucket instead of blanking the header.
